grades.quote: If the scheduler later schedules each thread on the opposite processor, most memory accesses will miss in the local cache and need to use the cache coherence protocol to retrieve data from the other cache.
grades.reason: Directly explains that migration loses local cache hits and requires retrieving data from another processor’s cache.
Discusses cache pollution from zero-filling pages, not thread migration between CPUs.

grades.quote: If one of the other processors now wants to write, the block needs to be flushed out of the first cache and loaded exclusively into the second. If the two processors keep alternately writing into the same block, there will be continual traffic on the memory interconnect as the cache block is transferred back and forth between the two caches.
grades.reason: Explains interprocessor cache-transfer costs, a useful mechanism underlying migration overhead, without directly discussing migration.

grades.quote: Because each miss necessitates an access to the slower main memory, the high rate of conflict misses will significantly reduce performance.
grades.reason: Provides background on why cache misses hurt performance, but does not explain why CPU migration causes them.
